Let me think about this more carefully. In Level 1, the white diamond was the "player" that moved along a path when clicking on objects. The goal was to get the white diamond to the purple ring (the last object on the path).
In Level 2, I see:
- White diamond at top-left (6,17)
- Orange circle at (12,24)
- Dark gray diamond at top-right (9,49)
- Dark gray diamond at middle-left (21,8)
- Dark gray diamond at middle-right (35,45)
- Purple square at (41,49)
- Dark gray diamond at bottom-right (48,54)
- Orange diamond at bottom-center (48-54, 37-43)
- Purple ring at middle-right (15-21, 54-60)
The light gray paths connect:
- White diamond → orange circle → dark gray diamond (TR)
- Dark gray diamond (ML) → ... (seems disconnected from white diamond)
Looking at the adjacency:
- White diamond (ID 6) is adjacent to: O(1px - its center), B(2747px - background)
- Orange circle (ID 14) is adjacent to: M(1px - center), w(2px), B, w(1px) - connected to path segments
- Gray diamond TR (ID 8) is adjacent to: w(2px), O(1px - center), B
So the white diamond is NOT directly connected to the path segments! It's only adjacent to its center pixel and the background. This is different from Level 1 where the white diamond was connected to the path.
Wait, but in Level 1, clicking on objects moved the white diamond. Maybe the same mechanic applies here. Let me try clicking on the orange circle to see if the white diamond moves there.
Actually, let me reconsider. In Level 1, the white diamond started OFF the path (at the left), and clicking on the purple ring (first object on path) moved it there. Then clicking on the next object moved it further.
In Level 2, the white diamond is at the top-left. The orange circle is the next object along the path. Let me try clicking on the orange circle.
